Package net.sourceforge.plantuml.teavm.browser

Class TeaVmFileLoader

java.lang.Object
net.sourceforge.plantuml.teavm.browser.TeaVmFileLoader
public final class TeaVmFileLoader extends Object
Reads the file of a local !include, !include_once, !include_many or !includesub, or of a !theme ... from a local folder, in the browser engine, through a function the host provides.

The browser engine has no file system, so on its own such an include can only fail. A host that does have files (an editor extension, a desktop application, a documentation build running the engine) sets PLANTUML_FILE_LOADER on the global object: 

 globalThis.PLANTUML_FILE_LOADER = function (path, from, onOk, onErr) { ... };
  • path: the file name the directive asks for, after variables are expanded and a selector (file!tag) is split off; for !theme NAME from DIR, DIR/puml-theme-NAME.puml. It is handed over as it is: the engine resolves nothing.
  • from: the file whose include is being resolved — null for the diagram itself, otherwise the identifier the host gave to the delivered file being evaluated, so that a relative name can be resolved against that file. A local theme keeps its caller's from for directives in its body, matching the Java build: null if the diagram called it, or the calling file's identifier. A standard-library file or a bundled theme being evaluated never asks the host (see PathSystem.withoutHostFiles()).
  • onOk(id, text): delivers the file. id is any non-empty string that identifies it for the host (typically its absolute path or URI), compared as it is. The include strategies count the identifier together with the selector, so two diagrams of one file are two includes. The body of an include or an includesub uses this identifier as from; a local theme instead keeps its caller's context.
  • onErr(reason): the include fails. The reason is written to the console.
The first outcome wins: a second callback, an exception or a rejection after it changes nothing. Returning false (strictly) before either callback declines the file, which then fails as if no loader were set, and a callback arriving later is ignored. A loader may be an async function: the rejection of the promise it returns fails the include, while the value it fulfils with is ignored, so a file is only ever delivered through onOk. A host that neither calls a callback, nor returns false, nor rejects, leaves the rendering waiting: there is no timeout in the engine. The engine never reads anything itself: which files may be read is decided by the host.

The same shape as PLANTUML_STDLIB_LOADER in TeaVmScriptLoader. With no loader set, a local include fails, and so does an includesub of a file, which used to be ignored in the browser. An includesub of a section in the diagram itself needs no loader.

  • Method Details

    • getInputFile

      public static InputFile getInputFile(String path, NFolder folder)
      The file the host delivers for path, or null when no loader is set, when the host declines, or when it fails (the reason is written to the console, and the include then reports the usual "cannot include"). Blocks until the host answers, so it MUST be called from a TeaVM thread context, like TeaVmScriptLoader.loadOnceSync(String).
      Parameters:
      path - the file name the directive asks for
      folder - where the include is written: null for the diagram itself, or the folder of a file this loader delivered. Any other folder has no host to ask.

    • getId

      public static String getId(InputFile file)
      The identifier the host gave to a file this loader delivered, or null for any other file. It is what an include strategy compares, as it is: two identifiers are the same file only when the strings are equal.
